Why every stored keyframe stays in the loss (RB2) and not S3, by source, not by score: KinectFusion (Newcombe et al., ISMAR 2011, sec. 3.3, Eq. 10-12; original text checked): 'The global fusion of all depth maps in the volume is formed by the weighted average of all individual TSDFs computed for each depth map', Eq. 10 min_F sum_k ||W_Rk (F_Rk - F)||^2, 'the solution can be obtained incrementally as more data terms are added using a simple weighted running average' (Eq. 11-12), 'by truncating the updated weight over some value'. TSDF fusion is the joint optimum over all frames, each once; the incremental form keeps the old frames' terms in F_{k-1}, W_{k-1}. The 3DGS counterpart keeps every keyframe's term in the loss; dropping the old terms (S3) has no counterpart, since GaME's optimizer has no prior term for them. The GT-free readings (A's readings within 5 cm of B-confirmed surfaces on 52 %; 21 % outside the band) call for the cross-session error model on those terms (the fork: error_per_metre q), not for dropping them.
